subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: Should sandboxed subagent startup failures remain accepted asynchronously and terminalize with a typed/logged failure, or should `sessions_spawn` preflight Docker startup enough to reject before returning accepted?
rationale: The choice affects the public async spawn contract, registry state, gateway waits, session projections, and the overlapping startup lifecycle PR, so automation should not pick the permanent behavior alone.

options.title: Terminalize Async Startup Failure
options.body: Keep the accepted response contract and add a typed logged terminal startup failure visible in session history, subagent list, and agent wait.

options.title: Preflight Sandbox Before Accept
options.body: Move enough Docker startup validation before acceptance to reject immediately, accepting extra latency and compatibility implications.

options.title: Defer To Lifecycle Tracker
options.body: Keep this issue open as the sandbox-specific repro while resolving the broader startup lifecycle direction in the related open lifecycle issue and PR.

recommendation.title: Terminalize Async Startup Failure
recommendation.body: Keep the accepted response contract and add a typed logged terminal startup failure visible in session history, subagent list, and agent wait.

likelyOwner.reason: The original sessions_spawn and sandbox visibility history makes this the best available owner for the API/behavior contract choice.
